newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed sharply lower as doubts about European economic and monetary union (EMU) continued to pound German bunds.
The sell-off was more marked than in Germany with the Dutch yield discount being trimmed by several basis points among 10 year and longer benchmarks.
The guilder yield curve between two and 10 years finished slightly steeper despite some institutional investors stepping back into the market to buy paper maturing 2005 and 2007.
"We saw some buying in the long end," said one trader, identifying demand for the new Feb 2007 benchmark bond.

Bunds were hit by more EMU comments, with Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher saying today that EMU would have to be delayed if Germany could not strictly meet the Maastrict Treaty criteria for entry to EMU.
He also said Germany was unlikely to meet the targets.
Concerns about the chances of German qualifying for EMU have grown recently, undermining the German mark-bloc which includes the Netherlands.
The yield on the Dutch 10-year benchmark rose for the fifth successive trading day, ending at 5.79 percent, compared with a record closing low of 5.38 percent on February 18.
The Dutch market rallied in the early afternoon after U.S. February housing starts data, but the gains were soon wiped out.
"We have seen a little money coming in at lower levels," said another dealer.
He also noted extension trades, with 2005 and 2006 paper benefitting from the buying.
The dealer said some Dutch funds had cash to spend after sitting on the sidelines in recent days, although most were fully invested.
"It's terribly quiet out there," he said.
